correctness.rationale: Reassessed the repaired whole-kernel claim. Independent polynomial spectral projectors at 0, 2−√2, 2, 2+√2 recover the distance-two, endpoint, and both adjacent-vertex formulas; reflection and positive semidefiniteness of the projectors handle the remaining entries. In scaled time the derivative of the distance-two entry after multiplication by exp(wτ) is strictly increasing from a negative value to infinity, since q^α−r^α>√2. The entry starts at zero and tends to 1/4, proving its unique positive crossing. The endpoint theorem has exactly the same generator, normalization and entry. Its crossing counts also follow from strict convexity of the rescaled endpoint derivative, the sign of the first Taylor coefficient (second at α=2), and negativity at scaled time log 2. The repaired explicit tests give D(log 2),E(log 2)<0 and D(2)>0>E(2) for α≥2. Hence the initial endpoint-positive window above two is blocked by the distance-two negativity, and the zeros create exactly the stated closed recovery ray and isolated time zero. For 1<α<2 both negative intervals start at zero, so their maximum sets the threshold. Fixed positive bracketing points on either side of the simple limiting zeros isolate the two early roots; in the a^αt time variable, brackets eventually lie beyond scaled time 2 and identify the late root only. This verifies the three limiting constants without assuming uniformity at the origin.
residual_risks: Applicable only to the precise unit combinatorial path; finite root grids would not give this all-exponent classification.

evidence: General eventual-positivity results and the constant spectral projector imply late positivity, not the transient ordering. Gregorio–Mugnolo prove eventual irreducibility at spectral power two on finite connected graphs, not the first globally nonnegative time on P4.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing broad results supply asymptotic positivity or a local-in-exponent analogue but do not mechanically imply the comparison tests, all-exponent overlap of the negative intervals, or the two distinct spectral rates in the large-exponent regime.

value.rationale: The sign of an individual entry is not enough to decide whether diffusion preserves the positive cone. In the shortest unweighted path with a distance-three pair, the distance-two crossings eliminate a possible early nonnegative window despite endpoint reentrance. The exact overlap test and late recovery scale quantify that distinction for every superunit exponent, with the two early events shown to share one scale. This is meaningful beyond reproducing the known endpoint classification.
residual_risks: No extension of the strict ordering to arbitrary edge weights or longer paths is shown.
